subject: Cooking
title: Pasteurization: The Heat That Saves Millions
description: A quick, practical guide to Pasteurization: The Heat That Saves Millions.

hook.text: In the 1860s, French wine kept spoiling in bottles. Louis Pasteur discovered why — and how to stop it.

buildup.text: Pasteur found that heating wine to 140°F killed the microbes causing spoilage without ruining flavor.

discovery.text: Applied to milk, pasteurization reduced infant mortality dramatically in the early 20th century.

twist.text: Ultra-high temperature (UHT) pasteurization heats milk to 280°F for 2 seconds — it lasts months unrefrigerated.

climax.text: Today pasteurization protects juice, eggs, beer, and even almonds from invisible threats.

punchline.text: Pasteur didn't invent preservation. He proved heat was enough.

quiz.question: What problem was Pasteur originally trying to solve?

details.summary: Pasteurization heats food to a specific temperature for a set time to kill dangerous pathogens without destroying the food. Louis Pasteur developed the technique in the 1860s. Milk pasteurized at 161°F for 15 seconds kills 99.999 percent of harmful bacteria while preserving nutrition and flavor.
details.whyItMatters: Pasteurization is one of the most important public health interventions in history. It makes milk, juice, and other beverages safe to drink on a massive scale.
takeaways: Time and temperature combinations kill pathogens predictably
HTST pasteurizes milk at 161°F for just 15 seconds
UHT processing at 280°F enables shelf-stable milk for months

faq.question: Does pasteurization destroy nutrients in milk?
faq.answer: Pasteurization reduces some heat-sensitive vitamins like C and B12 by 10 to 20 percent. However, milk is not a significant source of these vitamins. Calcium, protein, and fat are unaffected. The health benefits of eliminating pathogens far outweigh minor nutrient losses.

faq.question: What is the difference between pasteurized and UHT milk?
faq.answer: Standard pasteurization at 161°F for 15 seconds requires refrigeration and lasts two to three weeks. UHT processing at 280°F for two seconds sterilizes milk completely, allowing sealed shelf storage for six to nine months without refrigeration.
